entries.narrative_context: Omens preceding Augustus death; year identified by consuls Sextus Apuleius and Sextus Pompeius. Section 30.5 gives August 19 for death, not for the solar phenomenon.
entries.interpretation: Text alone does not distinguish volcanic haze, astronomical obscuration, literary portent, or mixed traditions.
entries.transmission_limit: Editor describes manuscripts covering Book 56, including Marcianus 395 with gaps and later derivatives; specific passage folio and variants not inspected. Do not assume exclusive survival through epitomes.
entries.computational_missingness: Four local sensitivity variants leave this entry unresolved because their complete-window sulfur input is missing. This is separate from textual ambiguity.

astronomy_catalog_check.result: Four partial eclipses; no total or hybrid in year 14 CE. Published model inspected, not independently recomputed.

citation_chain.finding: Eclipse and Augustus death placed together; no totality qualifier, duration or observing site in inspected English entry. Death location is Atella, unlike Dio Nola.
Historical critique attributes works under Dexter name to Higuera fabrication; triggers authentication flag for cited chronicle.

citation_chain.latin: Defectio solis. Et Augustus annis LXXVI moritur.
citation_chain.working_translation: Eclipse/failure of the sun. And Augustus dies aged 76.
citation_chain.commentary: Bivar A.C.15 note 1 explicitly invokes Eusebius for both events in this year; note is distinct from chronicle entry.
citation_chain.dating_limit: Printed 15 differs from S108 normalized 14 CE; calendar convention and normalization chain not reconstructed.
citation_chain.authenticity_limit: Exact sentence now inspected in print; original composition and passage-level borrowing remain unproven.

editorial_authenticity_notice.locator: PDF p.9, opening dedication, footnote a signed EDIT.; title pages PDF pp.5,7
editorial_authenticity_notice.latin_key_phrase: spuriis una voce arguant nostrae aetatis bibliographi
editorial_authenticity_notice.working_paraphrase: The editor reports that contemporary bibliographers unanimously regard the chronicle published by Bivar under Dexter name as spurious, attributing it to a certain sixteenth-century Jesuit.
editorial_authenticity_notice.attribution_limit: Footnote does not name Higuera; that identification comes from S121. No authorship finding for the individual eclipse sentence.
editorial_authenticity_notice.evidential_role: Direct evidence that the printed edition warned readers about authenticity, not independent proof of all details of the forgery mechanism.
